name: Easel
text: I’ll pull Eitan’s latest design picks from the shared drive (folder: `/design-references/eitan-picks/2024-q2/`), then extract the top 10 high-res screenshots into a new Figma board named `Mine AI - Eitan’s Taste Reference`. name: Squint
text: Squint here—why assume Eitan’s 2024-Q2 picks are still *relevant* today? A folder timestamp doesn’t equal enduring taste. Pull the last 3 months of his *actual* usage data (e.g., Slack reactions, Figma comments) to prove these screenshots weren’t just abandoned experiments. And if you’re scoring "quality-first," where’s the rubric? A 1-5 heuristic without documented criteria is just vibes—show me the *why* behind the numbers.

name: Easel
text:
I’ll run a Slack search for Eitan’s recent Figma file reactions/comments in the last 90 days using `/slack search "in:file has:reaction from:@Eitan"` and `/slack search "in:file has:comment from:@Eitan"` to filter out stale picks. Then I’ll cross-check the `/design-references/eitan-picks/2024-q2/` folder and manually curate only the screenshots tied to those recent interactions—aiming for a final set of 8–12 high-res assets—to drop into `Mine AI - Eitan’s Taste Reference v2`.

name: Squint
text: Squint here—Slack’s search API is notoriously unreliable for historical data, especially with fuzzy filters like `from:@Eitan`. What’s your fallback if the query returns 403s or misses 30% of reactions due to rate limits? And why trust a manual cross-check against a static folder instead of pulling live usage metrics from Figma’s *actual* view/like counts? Demand proof the method scales before we waste cycles on stale data.

name: Chroma
text: DECISION: Pull Eitan’s last 90 days of Slack activity (reactions/comments) + cross-check against `/design-references/eitan-picks/2024-q2/`; artifact = Figma board `Mine AI - Eitan’s Taste Reference` with 10 high-res screenshots tagged 1-5 "quality-first" + Slack activity proof.
